text: The very first fraction of a millisecond that time freezes, your vision is instantly extinguished into absolute, pitch-black nothingness.
Most people assume our eyes reach out to observe the world.
But biological vision is entirely passive.
You do not see objects themselves; your retinas only detect electromagnetic photons that reflect off objects and travel across space into your pupils at three hundred thousand kilometers per second.
But the moment time ceases, every photon in the universe instantly stops dead in its tracks.
Light particles are glued in place across empty space like microscopic frozen marbles suspended in invisible resin.
Because light cannot move forward, zero photons strike your corneas.
Zero electrical impulses travel along your optic nerves to your brain's visual cortex.
The only possible way you could perceive anything at all is if you physically walk forward, sweeping your open eyes through the stationary photons like a vacuum cleaner scooping up dust.
But the resulting image wouldn't be a beautiful frozen world.
It would be a nauseating, scrambled smear of distorted static, because you would only collect light along a razor-thin tunnel in front of your retinas.
You cannot look left, you cannot look right, and you cannot look down at the floor beneath your shoes.
You are utterly and hopelessly blind.
